title: Homeowner is about to sign a six-figure renovation contract without knowing the real permit path
job: Commit to scope, team, price and sequence without avoidable permit or change-order risk.
trigger: Contractor asks for deposit or contract signature.
surfaceComplaint: The quotes are wildly different and everyone gives me a different answer about permits.
mechanism: Quotes encode different scopes, exclusions, sequencing assumptions and permit responsibilities. The owner commits before these assumptions are normalized.

actors.incentive: finish legally, on time and budget

economics.painCostNote: One missed scope or permit dependency can create thousands in change orders and weeks of delay.

buyer.roiLogic: Small relative to a C$30k-300k project.

distribution.acquisition: Intercept before deposit, not after construction starts.

competitors.gap: vendor is not neutral and scopes differ
may not compare contractor commercial assumptions

experiment.sample: 8 homeowners with 2+ quotes and no signed contract
experiment.success: 4/8 pay C$750+ and half surface >C$5k quote/scope differences or material permit dependency
experiment.kill: owners consistently rely on existing GC/architect and will not pay independently

claims.text: Toronto holds homeowners responsible for required permits even if a contractor advises otherwise.
The highest-value intervention likely occurs before deposit, when assumptions are reversible.
